title: Perceive Once, Escalate on Demand: Handing Off Visual KV Memory from Small to Large VLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.26902v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: An embodied agent cannot afford a large vision-language model (VLM) at every step of a long video, so a cascade runs a small VLM continuously and escalates only uncertain decisions to a large one. Each escalation, however, forces the large model to re-encode a history the small model has already perceived, and this dominates its cost. We present Baton, which hands the large model the small model's visual memory, its key-value (KV) cache over the history. Baton rests on one finding: the large model needs a usable memory, not a faithful copy of its own. A map trained to reproduce the large model's cache matches it most closely, yet brings no gain over the small model alone. Baton instead distills a per-layer linear map, without labels, from the large model's own answers, with the large model encoding only the current frame. Interventions on the map trace the gain to one direction, carried by the middle third of the large model's layers.

translated_title: 感知一次，按需升级：将视觉KV记忆从小型VLM传递给大型VLM
translated_abstract: 具身智能体无法在长视频的每一步都负担得起大型视觉语言模型（VLM），因此级联系统持续运行一个小型VLM，仅将不确定的决策升级给大型模型。然而，每次升级都迫使大型模型重新编码小型模型已经感知过的历史信息，这占据了其主要成本。我们提出了Baton，它将小型模型的视觉记忆——即其在历史信息上的键值（KV）缓存——交给大型模型。Baton基于一个发现：大型模型需要一个可用的记忆，而不是自身缓存的忠实副本。一个训练用于重现大型模型缓存的映射虽然与它最为接近，但相比单独使用小型模型却没有任何收益。Baton转而从大型模型自身的答案中无标签地蒸馏出一个逐层线性映射，大型模型只需编码当前帧。对该映射的干预实验将增益追溯到由大型模型中间三分之一层所携带的一个方向。
tldr: 提出Baton方法，通过从大型模型自身答案中无标签蒸馏逐层线性映射，将小型VLM的视觉KV缓存记忆传递给大型VLM，避免升级时重复编码历史信息，使大型模型只需编码当前帧。
en_tdlr: Baton distills a label-free per-layer linear map from the large model's own answers to hand off the small VLM's visual KV memory, eliminating costly history re-encoding during cascade escalation so the large model only needs to encode the current frame.
